2 - Disciplinary Procedure/Conduct of Spectators (League & Cup) & Appeal Process
General Information 
Disciplinary thresholds remain unchanged from the previous season and apply to both league and cup competitions. 
Points System 

Yellow Card - 2 points 

Red Card - 4 points 
Note: Two yellow cards in a single match, resulting in a red card, count as 4 points in total. 
Suspension Deferrals 

If a player reaches a disciplinary threshold that would cause them to miss a cup final due to an earlier caution, 
the suspension will be deferred. 

However, if a player receives a red card for violent conduct or serious foul play, the suspension will stand, and 
the player will be ineligible for the final. 
 
Disciplinary Thresholds 
Threshold 
Points 
Suspension 
1 
10 points 
1-match suspension (plus any red card suspension) 
2 
18 points 
3-match suspension (plus any red card suspension) 
3 
24 points 
5-match suspension (plus any red card suspension) 
4 
28 points 
7-match suspension (plus any red card suspension) 
5 
30 points 
10-match suspension (plus any red card suspension) 
 
Serious Offences 

Foul and Abusive Language (towards opponent): 
3-match ban 

Foul and Abusive Language (towards an official): 
o
1st Offe nce: 5-match ban 
o
2nd Offe nce: 1-year ban (to be reviewed before eligibility to return) 

Discriminatory Language: 
o
1st Offe nce: 10-match ban 
o
2nd Offe nce: 1-year ban (to be reviewed before eligibility to return) 

Violent Conduct (e.g. kicking, punching): 
o
Minimum 1 year ban.
o
Review required before returning 
o
Repeat Offe nce: Lifetime ban 
Note: All red card offences will be assessed individually. Disciplinary records from previous seasons will be considered, 
and repeat offenders may face extended bans or expulsion from the league for persistent poor conduct. 
 
Team Disciplinary Penalties 

20+ disciplinary points across 4 consecutive matches: Mike Egan (Or) Linesmen for 3 matches, at a cost to the 
team under disciplinary review.
Most teams remain well below these limits. Maintaining good conduct while playing competitively is achievable and 
encouraged. 
 
Appeals Process 

Only lifetime bans may be appealed. 

Appeals must be submitted by the team manager, with supporting evidence of improved behaviour (e.g., 
discipline records from other leagues).

Behaviour Expectations 
All players, managers, coaches, and spectators are expected to uphold the values and ethos of the Church League at all times - 
during league matches, cup games, friendlies, and social events. 
If any individual is found using obscene or intimidating language, or behaving disruptively to the point a referee must 
abandon a match, the league (in consultation with the lead referee) may: 

Order a replay on neutral ground, or 

Award a win to the opposing team 
Further disciplinary action may also be taken. 
 
Playing / Attending Matches While Banned in ECFA League 
If a player under suspension in the ECFA League plays: 

The ir ban will be doubled automatically 

The  match result will be overturned to a 3-0 loss for the offending team 

If the team already lost, the opposition can choose between keeping the result or receiving a 3-0 awarded win 
If a player attends a game and is serving a serious ban (four or more games); 

The  team may receive a one-point deduction from their league total 

The ir ban will be doubled automatically 
 
The  onus is on the manager of each team to communicate all of the above when discussing bans with players, teams.

7 - Referee Notes & Agreement
ECFA League Agreement - 2026/27 Season 
This agreement outlines the expectations and terms for referees offic iating regularly within the Edinburgh Churches 
Football Association (ECFA) League. It has been reviewed and approved by the ECFA League Committee. 
General Referee Responsibilities 

Match Assignments: 
Committee will assign all fixtures to referees. 

Pitch Inspections: 
If multiple fixtures are scheduled near your home, you may be requested to carry out a pitch inspection the evening 
before or morning of the game. 
o
A petrol allowance of £10 will be provided for inspections, payable via bank transfer. 

Match Fees: 
o
Standard match fee: £55 per game, to be collected from the away team. 
o
Cup matches with extra time/penalties: Fee remains £55, unless otherwise agreed on the day by both 
teams. 
o
Postponed due to weather: No fee is payable. 
o
Postponed due to a team not showing up: Referee may receive £55, at the referee’s discretion. 

Availability and Communication: 
o
If unable to offic iate a scheduled match, notify the chat immediately. 
o
Referees are primarily assigned to matches within Edinburgh, but may occasionally be asked to travel to 
nearby outskirts. 
o
Midweek matches may be held outside Edinburgh; you will only be expected to offic iate once the venue has 
been confirmed and agreed upon. 
Match Reporting and Conduct 

Score Reporting: 
o
For Saturday matches, the score must be posted in the group chat by 6:00 PM the same day.

ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  5
o
For midweek matches, the score must be shared by 6:00 PM the following day. 

Disciplinary Reporting: 
o
All yellow and red cards must be reported via the group chat. 
o
If necessary, a written incident report may be required for serious matters. 

Match Day Procedures: 
o
Referees will wear a kit colour different from both teams, based on pre-match communication. 
o
The  ECFA does not use team lines, so referees are expected to record player names rather than 
numbers. 
o
Referees should monitor substitutions, recording the jersey numbers of all players entering the field. 
Substitution and Squad Rules 

Maximum squad size: 18 players. 

Maximum of five substitutions per team is allowed. 

Rolling substitutions are permitted only if both teams agree and have informed the referee prior to kick-
off 
o
While the ECFA's default stance is against rolling subs, mutual agreement between both teams overrides this 
for individual matches. 
o
If a team is reduced to 10 men due to injuries, they can bring on a player already subbed off, this is regardless 
of an agreement of rolling subs and is an agreement between all managers in the league. 
 
League Ethos and Behaviour 

The  ECFA is a church-led league. Some teams may choose to pray before kick-off 

Teams are expected to uphold the Christian ethos and values of the league. 

If a referee has concerns regarding a team’s conduct or general behaviour, they are encouraged to inform the 
league directly. 
 
Referee Contact Information 
Please complete the following details:

Full Name: 

Address:


Email Address: 

First Aid Trained: Yes / No

10 - Indefin ite Ban Procedure
Can only be appealed once, which must occur at least 12 months afte r the ban was imposed. 
Appeals must be submitted by the team manager, with supporting evidence of improved behaviour (e.g., discipline 
records from other leagues). 
The  league may request additional information and consult with relevant church representatives, not just the team 
manager. 
Disciplinary Thresholds - Returning Players 
Threshold 
Points 
Suspension 
1 
6 points 
1-match suspension 
2 
10 points 
3-match suspension 
3 
14 points 
5-match suspension 
Note: 
Upon reaching 14 points, the player and the manager / Church Rep will discuss the reasons for the high disciplinary 
points with the league committee and review the nature of the cards received. This review may lead to the 
reintroduction of an indefinite ban. 
11- Postponement of Matches
All teams are entitled to request one postponement of a game if they are unable to field a squad, however it is the team 
who is cancelling the matches responsibility to contact the fixture organiser, opposition and referee before Monday the 
week of the match when a Saturday, and if a midweek match at least 3 working days to stop any additional costs being 
passed to the team. Cancelled games will be aimed to be played at a later date in the season rather than an automatic 
walkover being handed to the team who hasn’t forfeited that game. If it’s an exceptional circumstance and a date for the 
game to be rescheduled cannot be found, then the team requesting the postponement will forfeit the Tie/Points.

Team Withdraws/expelled and Player Movement

ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  9
If a team withdraws/is expelled from the league, all previously played matches will stand, but all future fixtures will be 
recorded as 3-0 forfeits in favour of the opposition, effe ctive from the date of the team's withdrawal. 
Players from a withdrawn team are free to join other ECFA teams and participate in all competitions, subject to the 
following conditions: 
The  April 1st player registration rule remains in effect. Players registering afte r April 1st will not be eligible for cup 
matches or designated key league games, regardless of the team’s withdrawal. 
Suspensions and bans will carry over to the player's new team and commence from the date of their new registration. 
Example: If a team folds on March 3rd and a player with a 3-match ban joins a new team on March 20th, the ban will 
begin on March 20th and apply to the next three matches for that player. 
A maximum of Three players from a withdrawn team may join a single team during the same season. 
If additional players wish to join a team that has already accepted three players from the withdrawn team, they must 
wait until the following season to register with that team. 
17 - League Trophies


Home team to contact ref & opposition once pitch is booked and advise of strip colour. This must be done by 6:00 PM 
on Thursday at the latest. 

All teams to advise Ian Midwinter Close of Play Tuesday if unable to fulfil a fixture, failure to do this will result 
in a forfeit and a 3-0 loss, and team may need to pay cost of park (if within 48 hours) and referee on the day. 

Teams can request one postponement per season, however must inform Iain McCalman before Monday the 
week of the match when a Saturday, and if a midweek match at least 3 working days to stop any additional costs being 
passed to the team.

Any refs unable to take a game must contact Greg Healey as soon as possible so he can find a replacement. 

Liam Burns advises teams of suspension period. 

Maximum Squad of 18 

Only 5 subs can be used (Regardless of rolling or not), it’s up to each team manager to communicate to their 
squad if they have more than 16 then some players will not get on. 

Both teams must agree rolling subs and confirm with the referee prior to kick off, if one team does not agree,

Home team brings nets & match ball

Home team puts nets up (Temporary rule until the next meeting)

Home team must pay the referee his fee by 6pm the same day of the game, either by bank transfer, or cash on 
the day. 

Away team must pay the home team their share (50%) of the fees by Thursday evening 11pm. 
Post-Match 

Both teams to send Iain list of scorers from the match (League matches only) 

Home team to send Iain (WhatsApp chat) the matchday score by 2pm the day of the game, 11pm for midweek 
matches. 

Referee to send any yellow/reds to Greg Healey and result of game into the referee chat. 
19 - ECFA Code of Conduct
Edinburgh Churches Football Association is a church led, Christian league that aims to provide an 
environment where competitive football is played in a manner that reflects Christian values. We 
welcome players of all backgrounds regardless of faith but expect that those associated with each club 
are sympathetic to our values and adhere to this code of conduct.

EDINBURGH CHURCHES FOOTBALL ASSOCIATION
10
ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  10
We expect that management teams will attempt to develop a settled squad, build relationships, and foster an 
environment that will lead to opportunities to witness.
As part of this purpose, we strongly discourage teams from bringing players in from outside of their existing squad 
without the prior approval of the opposition and league chairman, and we will not permit the use of ‘ringers’ for any 
fixture. That is, players deemed to have been brought in to strengthen a team beyond its usual squad resources to 
increase their chances of winning a fixture or progressing in a competition.
Clubs found to have acted in this manner will be subject to disciplinary proceedings, including the 
forfeiture of the result or expulsion from competition.
Playing under the banner of Edinburgh Churches Football Association comes with certain expectations and responsibilities 
which players, management and supporters of each club will be asked to respect and support whilst participating in matches 
and events this season.
At all times play hard but fair - giving 100% effort, remembering that it’s not only the result but also HOW we play that 
matte rs.
Team-mates, the opposition and referees must be treated with the utmost respect.
‘Simulation’ or ‘Gamesmanship’ is cheating and will not be tolerated in this league. No attempt should be made to wind 
up or incite a player or mislead a referee.
Control your language, watch what you say! - Foul and abusive language spoils the image of the league, and negative 
comments affect the spirit within each team.
During a game, only the captain and manager can speak to the referee. Any grievances should be taken to the captain. 
Always play to the whistle and accept the referees’ decision as final.
Those involved on the side-lines are not to get involved in referee's decisions. No abuse should be directed towards 
anyone involved on either side or the referee.
Exercise Sportsmanship in all situations, gracious in victory and dignified in defeat.
Physical violence will not be tolerated at any level and will result in disciplinary action, up to and including expulsion 
from the league.
As Manager and Representative of my club, I undertake to try and adhere to behavioural standards that are consistent 
with the Christian faith and encourage all those associated with my club to follow these practices
20 - League Registration & Criteria (New Applicants) 
The  Edinburgh Churches Football Association (ECFA) is a church-led, Christian league committe d to providing a competitive 
football environment that refle cts Christian values. 
We welcome players from all backgrounds, regardless of faith. However, it is expected that all individuals associated 
with a club are sympathetic to these values and agree to abide by the ECFA Code of Conduct. 
We expect management teams to strive toward developing a settled and stable squad, promoting positive 
relationships and fostering an environment that encourages opportunities to witness. 
 
New Team Application Process 
To join the ECFA, prospective teams must meet the following criteria: 
1.
Application Submitted with letter from the current minister of the church, and agreed support model.
2.
Initial Meeting with ECFA Leadership 
All managers must meet with the ECFA Chairman or a designated representative prior to acceptance. This meeting will 
focus on the ethos and purpose of the team, ensuring alignment with the league's values and structure. 
o
Following the meeting, the Chairman may recommend to the league that the application be declined if the 
team is not a suitable fit. 
2.
Code of Conduct Agreement 
All teams must formally agree to uphold and promote behaviours as outlined in the ECFA Code of Conduct. 
3.
Church Connection Confirmation 
A letter of confirmation and support must be submitted from the church with which the team is connected, affirming 
the relationship and backing the application. 
4.
Membership Vote 
The  application will be subject to a vote by existing member teams.

ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  11
o
Current members are encouraged to share any relevant experiences or knowledge of the applying team or its 
management. 
o

League Registration & Criteria (Existing Member Clubs) 
The  Edinburgh Churches Football Association (ECFA) is a church-led, Christian football league that strives to provide a 
competitive sporting environment grounded in Christian values. 
We welcome players of all backgrounds, regardless of faith, but expect all individuals associated with clubs to be 
respectful of our values and to comply with the ECFA Code of Conduct. 
We also expect management teams to work towards building a settled squad, nurturing strong relationships, and 
fostering an environment that encourages opportunities to witness through sport. 
 
New Season Application Requirements 
To be eligible for participation each season, teams must meet the following criteria: 
1.
Church Support Confirmation 
All managers must submit a letter of confirmation from their church, affirming continued support for the team’s 
participation in the upcoming season. 
2.
Code of Conduct Agreement 
All teams are required to sign and agree to adhere to the standards of behaviour set out in the ECFA Code of Conduct, 
and to actively promote these values within their team. 
3.
Loss of Church Support 
Any team that no longer has active support from a church may be required to reapply as a new team. In some cases, 
the team’s participation in the ECFA may be refused for the upcoming season.

22 - Match Abandonment Policy 
⚠️ Scenario 1: Misconduct by a Team 
If a match is abandoned by the referee due to the behaviour of one team, the following will apply: 

The  offe nding team will forfeit the match 3-0. 

If the score at the time of abandonment is higher than 3-0 in favour of the opposition (e.g. 4-0 or 4-1), that score will 
stand. 

Goal scorers from both teams may be recorded. 
🔍 Example: A match is abandoned at 4-1 due to misconduct. The  result stands as 4-1, and all goal scorers are logged. 
 Scenario 2: Abandonment Due to Weather or Injury 
If a match is abandoned due to external factors (e.g. severe weather, serious injury, or other unavoidable 
incidents): 

The  match will be rescheduled. 

Both managers will be consulted in the rescheduling process. 

The  point of abandonment may help determine whether a full replay is viable, especially considering costs 
and logistics. 
🔁 Replay decisions will take into account how far into the match the abandonment occurred and whether the remaining 
game time justifie s rescheduling.

24 - ECFA Transfers and Player Eligibility Policy 
1. Player Transfers - ECFA to ECFA 

It is the responsibility of each team manager to confirm that any incoming player has not previously played for 
more than one ECFA team in the current season.

EDINBURGH CHURCHES FOOTBALL ASSOCIATION

ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  13

If a player has already played for another ECFA team, the manager must contact the previous manager to 
confirm that the transfer is acceptable. 

A Player Transfer Form must be completed for all transfers between ECFA teams. Managers should request 
this form at the time of the player's move. 

All transfers where a player has played for an ECFA team before, will be posted into the ECFA WhatsApp channel.
2. Player Transfers - Amateur to ECFA 

Players currently registered and playing Saturday amateur football are not eligible to participate in the 
ECFA league.  Players may be asked for proof that they are no longer registered to a team (email from Comet received 
by player)

If an amateur player becomes unattached and wishes to join an ECFA team, the Player Transfer Form must 
include: 
o
The  name of their previous club. 
o
The  date they left that club. 
o
Any current suspensions or bans from other leagues, including the reason for the ban. 

The  league must be informed of any such circumstances. 

Has the player played for your team already this season (If so the league will need details and can   veto this 
move)
3. Junior, Semi-Professional, and Professional Players 

Players who are currently registered with junior, semi-professional, or professional teams are not 
eligible to play in the ECFA concurrently. 

If such a player leaves their club and wishes to join an ECFA team in the same season: 

The  manager must receive an email from the player received via comet to confirm they have been released.

A Player Transfer Form must be submitted. 
o
The  league will assess the transfer and discuss it directly with the team manager, and may seek further proof 
that the player is no longer registered.
4. Transfer Restrictions - April 1st Deadline and Cup Semi Finals and Finals

From April 1st onwards, teams may not register new players for: 
o
Cup matches, and 
o
Any identified key league fixtures (as determined by the league).

EDINBURGH CHURCHES FOOTBALL ASSOCIATION

ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  14

Players may still be registered afte r April 1st if they do not fall under any of the restrictions mentioned in sections 1-
3. 

Such players will be ineligible for both cup matches and key league fixtures afte r this date. 

Due to the ECFA Knockout Cup Final and Semi Finals taking place in the first half of the season, this rule has 
also been extended to the semi finals and final of this competition, any new additions added afte r the quarter final stage, 
will be ineligible to play in the semi final, and final of this competition.  Any team that plays players registered afte r this 
point will forfeit the tie and the opposition
5. Cup Tie Rule 

The  Cup Tie Rule has been removed due to changes surrounding post-April 1st transfers. 

However, to be eligible for Cup matches, players must be registered on the official squad list by April 
1st. 
6. Administrative Guidelines and Housekeeping 

The  ECFA operates on a trust-based system, minimising the need for extensive paperwork and matchday 
administration. 

Team managers are expected to maintain integrity and communicate openly, especially regarding player 
transfers. 

If unsure about any player’s eligibility, managers should contact the league or reach out via the official 
WhatsApp group. 

Transfer forms will be shared in the managers’ WhatsApp group to maintain transparency across all 
teams. 

Any team found to have violated these rules-with suffic ient evidence that a player was brought in to unfairly 
influence a game-will forfeit the match in question.
A player cannot play for more than two ECFA teams per season. In exceptional circumstances, a special request can be 
submitte d to the league for approval if a player has already transferred twice or appeared for two separate teams. 
25 - ECFA Squad Rules (2026/27 Season) 
Matchday Squad Sizes 

Teams may bring a maximum of 18 players to a match. 

Only 5 substitutions may be made during a game. 

If you bring more than 16 players, it is your responsibility to communicate clearly to the squad that not all 
players are guaranteed playing time.

EDINBURGH CHURCHES FOOTBALL ASSOCIATION
15
ECFA League Handbook 2026/27  |  15
 Substitutions 

Default Rule: Once a player is substituted off, they cannot return to the game. 

Rolling Subs: Permitted only if agreed by both teams prior to kick-offand communicated to the referee. 

Injury Exception: If a player is injured and leaves the team with 10 men, a previously substituted player may 
re-enter the match to replace the injured player. 
 
Trialist Rule (Removed 27/08/2025)
The re may be occasions where additional players are needed mid-season or new players express interest in joining. 
Please adhere to the following rules regarding trialists: 

A player may appear as a trialist in up to 3 matches per season. Afte r that, they must be registered to 
continue playing. 
Registration Deadline: All players must be registered by Thursday before a match, and 24 hours before a midweek 
match, Failure to do so will result in: 
o
A 3-0 forfeit if the offending team won the match. 
o
A 1-point deduction (with the result standing) if the offending team lost. 

Notification Requirements: 
o
The  opposition must be informed when trialists are fielded. 
o
The league must be notified with the following details: 

Full Name 

Date the player was fielded as a trialist 

Whether they have played for an ECFA team before 

Confirmation of eligibility 

When registering a new player permanently, also include: 
o
Whether the player is first-aid trained 

A maximum of 3 trialists is allowed in any matchday squad. 

Trialists may not play in: 
o
Cup matches 
o
Any match on or after April 1st each season. 

Please inform the league when a player is permanently removed from your squad. 
⚠️ Note: The  ECFA encourages the development of settled squads. Excessive use of trialists may result in review or 
action by the League Admin.
